question: Does an explicit sequence identity prevent temporal grain repetition and state carryover across unrelated shots while preserving deterministic replay and partition handoff within each shot?
forbidden: reuse a local frame index and unscoped seed across unrelated shots
carry exposure or gate-weave state across a shot boundary without an explicit same-sequence declaration
derive sequence identity from image content, timestamps, filenames or hidden target pixels
change identifiers, controls, frame counts or gates after formal scoring
claim synthetic state semantics establish measured transport behavior or video product quality

branch_rule.pass: retain explicit sequence-scoped temporal stream identities and shot-reset semantics as the reference contract
branch_rule.fail: close the sequence-state mechanism without seed, identifier, frame-count or threshold rescue

claim_ceiling: Synthetic deterministic shot-boundary state and counter-domain semantics only; not measured film transport, scene-cut detection, temporal image quality, arbitrary video support or product readiness.
